Use N, mm, MPa units throughout.
Model a straight cantilever beam of length L = 1800 mm, fixed at x = 0 and free at x = L.
Apply Euler-Bernoulli beam theory with small-deflection, linear-elastic assumptions.
The beam is made of structural steel with Young's modulus E = 200000 MPa.
The cross-section has constant second moment of area I = 1200000 mm^4.
A single downward point load P = 2000 N acts at the free end (x = L).
No distributed load, no applied couple, and no intermediate support exist along the span.
The bending moment in any cross-section is M(x) = P(L - x), varying linearly from PL at the fixed end to zero at the free end.
Compute the slope (rotation) at the free end using theta = P L^2 / (2 E I).
Compute the vertical deflection at the free end using delta = P L^3 / (3 E I).
Report the slope in radians (optionally also in degrees) and the deflection in mm, both positive in the direction of the applied load.
